# Historical Ground Truth: Coase — Transaction Costs × Property Rights

**Type**: real, historically-confirmed discovery — hand-authored calibration benchmark, **not generated by `hypothesis_engine.py`**
**Mode framing**: Bisociation (the discovery is presented in this pipeline's own bisociation shape for comparability, not because it was produced by the generator)
**Domains**: Coase — law and economics (transaction costs) × Property rights — resource allocation
**Source**: `bisociation_gold_pairs.json` (held-out batch, 2026-08-31), expanded into a precise technical claim for refutation-lens calibration (2026-08-31)

---

## The Core Claim

In the absence of transaction costs, the initial legal assignment of a property right does not affect the efficiency of the final allocation of resources -- bargaining parties trade to the value-maximizing outcome regardless of who is initially granted the right (the Coase theorem); real-world transaction costs (negotiation, enforcement, information) are precisely what make the initial legal assignment of rights matter in practice, explaining why firms and legal institutions exist at all as ways to economize on those costs. Ronald Coase won the 1991 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for this discovery of the significance of transaction costs and property rights for the institutional structure of the economy.
